data.name: Sorin
data.gender_notes: Sorin is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Roman name 'Sorinus', derived from the Latin word 'sorere' meaning 'to defend'. This name was borne by several early Christian saints. The name Sorin carries the meaning “Defender” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Sorin usually hope their child will grow to embody defender and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A guardian of faith and protector of the weak.
data.etymology: Sorin belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Defender.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Sorin total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

in_hebrew.name: סורין
in_hebrew.long_meaning: שם זה מקורו בשפה הרומנית, והוא נגזר מהמילה הלטינית 'soror' או 'soro' שפירושה אח, או 'sorin' שפירושו צעיר, והוא משמש כשם תיאופורי, המבטא את הקשר עם האל

in_greek.name: Σορίν
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα αυτό προέρχεται από τη ρουμανική γλώσσα, και είναι導 από τη λατινική λέξη 'soror' ή 'soro' που σημαίνει αδελφός, ή 'sorin' που σημαίνει νέος, και χρησιμοποιείται ως ονομα θεοφόρος, που εκφράζει τη σχέση με τον Θεό

in_latin.name: Sorin
in_latin.long_meaning: Hoc nomen originem habet in lingua romana, et derivatur a verbo latino 'soror' vel 'soro' quod significat fratrem, aut 'sorin' quod significat iuvenem, et utitur ut nomen theophorum, quod exprimit relationem cum Deo

in_english.name: Sorin
in_english.long_meaning: This name originates from the Romanian language, and is derived from the Latin word 'soror' or 'soro' meaning brother, or 'sorin' meaning young, and is used as a theophoric name, expressing the relationship with God, symbolizing spiritual kinship and youthful vitality

data.cultural_impact: The name "Sorin" has its roots in Roman culture, representing the ideas of strength, protection, and defense. Its association with early Christian saints suggests a deep-rooted connection to the preservation and safeguarding of faith and values. In various regions, this name became popular, contributing to the diverse cultural mosaic of Christian communities and beyond.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name "Sorin" lies in its associations with defending and preserving one's faith. As a Christian name, it is a reminder of the importance of standing firm in one's beliefs and upholding spiritual values. In a metaphorical sense, the name may inspire those bearing it to be spiritual protectors and defenders, safeguarding not just their own faith but also the faith and wellbeing of others. Overall, this name carries powerful symbolism embodying courage, resilience, and faith.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Sorin signifies "mountain of great joy" in Romanian, embodying the profound happiness found in the Christian faith and the strength found in God's presence.

historical_references.reference: Saint Sorin of Quercy, also known as Sorin of Cahors, was a 6th-century hermit and bishop. He is said to have lived as a hermit in the forest of Quercy in southwest France, and was later consecrated bishop of Cahors by Saint Expedite. Sorin is considered a patron saint of the city and is venerated in the diocese of Cahors.

Another Saint Sorin, also known as Sorin of Abbeville, was a 7th-century monk and bishop. He is believed to have been born in Auxerre, in northern France, and later became a monk at the Abbey of Saint-Germain-des-Prés in Paris. Sorin went on to found the Abbey of Saint-Savin-sur-Gartempe in Poitou, where he served as abbot. He was later consecrated bishop of Abbeville in Normandy and died there in 636.

It is frequently featured on social media platforms where parents share their naming journeys, and Christian name websites where expectant parents research meaningful Biblical names. The name bridges traditional Christian values with modern faith identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and Biblical significance.
